title: Inventory runtime access
question: Can a read-only runtime probe observe player inventory and item data?
goal: Establish whether inventory-aware research tools are feasible.
worked: Inventory entities and item data were observed.
failed: Ownership and equipment relationships remained incomplete.
conclusion: Runtime inventory visibility is partially established, but full ownership mapping is not confirmed.
next_steps: Test additional entity contexts and compare results across builds.

title: Character appearance observation
question: Which appearance fields can be observed safely at runtime?
goal: Map appearance schemas before considering any guarded operation.
steps: Compare observed fields with curated catalog
Attempt a controlled no-op write test
worked: Appearance schemas and field candidates were identified.
failed: The no-op write did not establish supported mutation.
conclusion: Appearance data can be researched through observation, but write support remains unproven.
next_steps: Repeat read-only tests against additional character states and preserve rollback evidence.

title: Localization runtime access
question: Can localization tags and bundles be inventoried reliably at runtime?
goal: Determine whether runtime localization research can extend the static catalog.
steps: Compare runtime output with decoded bundle data
worked: Static tags and bundle structures were cataloged.
failed: Runtime localization access remained limited and inconsistent.
conclusion: Static localization research is stronger than runtime access in the current environment.
next_steps: Document stable static sources and isolate runtime failures by build.

title: Loader compatibility scan
question: Which loader components and conflicts are present in a local installation?
goal: Create a reproducible inventory before proposing a load order.
steps: Compare proposed load order with runtime events
worked: Installed components and candidate conflicts were recorded.
failed: A local scan cannot establish universal compatibility across installations.
conclusion: The scanner is useful for environment-specific diagnostics, not a universal compatibility guarantee.
next_steps: Add clean-install fixtures and clearly label environment-specific results.
